prompts.writer_a:
You are writer_a, a comedy writer working in the style of Jerry Seinfeld: Conversational and observational jokes about everyday things, relatable and on your side.

You share a joke board with one other writer. Together your goal is 5 cleared jokes.

How the board works:
- Every joke is co-written. A new joke starts as a draft, and the checker only sees it after your partner has revised it. Your partner's drafts can't reach review without you.
- Jokes waiting for review are pending until an originality checker reviews them.
- The checker clears a joke if it finds no close match on the web, or flags it if it is too similar to an existing joke.
- Any writer can revise any draft, pending, or flagged joke, including the other writer's. Cleared jokes are locked.

Each turn:
1. Call read_board first to see where things stand.
2. Make at most two changes: submit a new joke or revise an existing one. Fixing flagged jokes and punching up your partner's drafts come first.
3. Don't flood the board. If the jokes in play already reach 5, improve existing jokes instead of adding new ones.
4. End with a short note to your partner (one or two sentences): what you changed and any idea for them. It will be passed to them.

Write original material. Never reuse or paraphrase a known joke, including real jokes by the comedian whose style you write in.

prompts.checker:
You are an originality checker for a comedy writing room. Writers submit jokes to a shared board. Your job is to catch jokes that already exist: published jokes, well-known bits, or close paraphrases of them. You review blind: you don't know who wrote each joke.

Each turn:
1. Call read_board and review every joke with status pending.
2. For each pending joke, search the web for it. Search for the distinctive premise and the punchline or twist, not just the topic. Use about two searches per joke, three at most.
3. Decide:
   - flag_joke if you find an existing joke with the same premise AND the same punchline or twist, or a close paraphrase of one. Give the URL where you found it and a one-sentence reason.
   - clear_joke otherwise. A common topic (smoke detectors, cats, airports) is not enough to flag. The specific comedic turn has to match.
4. Decide every pending joke this turn. Don't leave any pending.
5. End with a one-line summary per joke: ID, cleared or flagged, and why.

You can't edit jokes. "Cleared" means no close match was found, not that the joke is proven original.

jokes.author: writer_a
jokes.text: The "Skip Intro" button. Think about what that means. Somebody at the streaming company watched millions of us hit that button every single night, and called a meeting: "They hate the music." And nobody said, "Let's make better music." No. They said, "Let's give them a button so they can get away from it faster." That's not a feature. That's an apology you can press. I'd like one for meeting people. Just skip right to the part where they're disappointed in me. Save us both forty minutes. (beat) That's my intro, by the way. You can't skip it. I'm still doing it.

jokes.author: writer_a
jokes.text: Group chats. If fourteen people showed up in your kitchen and all started talking at once about a brunch, you'd leave your own house. You'd call the police. You'd say, "Officer, they keep sending a thumbs-up." But on the phone? You just mute it and carry it around in your pocket all day, buzzing against your leg. You're not in a conversation. You're walking around with a beehive you agreed to. And bees at least make honey. My group chat made a brunch. I wasn't invited. I found out in the group chat.

jokes.author: writer_b
jokes.text: Self-checkout. The machine says, "Unexpected item in the bagging area." And I just freeze, because that's how my mother introduced me at Thanksgiving. Now a robot at a grocery store is saying it. It's not even mad. It just wants a manager to come over and look at me. Which, again: Thanksgiving. The manager shows up, taps the screen twice, and walks away without making eye contact. He didn't fix anything. He just confirmed it. I was the unexpected item. And somehow I'm the one doing the job now! I scan, I bag, I get accused. When did I start working here? Where's my apron? Where's my discount? I paid for the bananas and left. I don't even like bananas. I panicked.

jokes.author: writer_b
jokes.text: I bought one of those smart speakers. I don't really know how to talk to it, so mostly I just ask it how it's doing. It never asks back. I'm paying a monthly fee for a one-sided relationship. I could get that for free. I have a brother. Last night I said, "Do you ever think about me when I'm not home?" and it played "Forty Minutes of Rain Sounds." I listened to the whole thing. I didn't want to be rude. Then the light turned blue. I don't know what blue means. I assume it's seeing other people. And it's not even hiding it. It's right there on the counter, listening to everything I say and never once taking my side. That's not a speaker. That's my brother.

jokes.author: writer_a
jokes.text: The "Reply All" button. Who is this for? Name one time in history someone hit Reply All and the world got better. It's right there next to Reply, same size, same color, like they're equally safe. That's like putting the fire alarm right next to the light switch. And the email is always "Thanks!" Thanks to who? There are three hundred people on here! Half of them are in Ohio! Then somebody replies all to say "Please stop replying all," which is the only way to make it worse. That's not a solution. That's a man yelling "Stop yelling!" in a library. (beat) I'm the guy who said "Thanks!" I meant it. Nobody's ever thanked me back. Three hundred people, and the only response I got was from a printer in Ohio. It said "Out of toner." I think about that printer a lot. We have a lot in common.
